name: WebSockets
plain: Opens a two-way live connection to a server, with no prompt.
meaning: A site can keep a persistent channel to its server for chat, live data or telemetry. It is not covered by CORS, and the connection ends when the tab closes.

web.api: new WebSocket('wss://...'); WebSocketStream (Chrome origin trial history)

access.persistence: Lives with the page; closed on unload; BFCache closes it
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Governed by CSP connect-src; no iframe flag needed
steps: Browser performs HTTP upgrade with Origin header

limits.headline: Can keep a live two way link to a server, with no pop up
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, like chat, live scores or games.
can: Send and get messages in both directions at once
Keep the link open while the page is open
Update the page right away with new data
cannot: Stay connected after you close the tab
Reach your files or other apps
Keep running well in a hidden tab; browsers may slow or drop it

story.what_it_is: A page can keep a live two way line open to a server, with no prompt.

marketing.name: WebSockets API
marketing.pitch: MDN says WebSockets let a page and a server send messages back and forth without repeated requests.

story.for_you: You never see it. Chat messages, live scores and multiplayer moves arrive the instant they happen, with no refresh.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for anything live: chat, trading, games, dashboards. It keeps a steady line open, which is faster than asking again and again.

use_cases.example: A browser shooter or io game sends your position to the server and gets everyone else's back many times a second.
A chat app delivers a message the second someone sends it.
A trading page streams live prices and fills.
Twitch chat flows through a live connection, so messages appear as they happen.
A shared doc editor sends every keystroke to teammates in real time.
A fraud tool streams behaviour signals from a login page to a scoring server as you type.

technical_bounds: Origin header is sent but no CORS check: servers must validate Origin
Mixed content: ws:// from an HTTPS page is blocked (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)
Per-host connection limits: Firefox 200 (network.websocket.max-connections); Chrome around 255 per renderer
Blocked ports list (about 70 ports such as 25, 110, 6667) applies
No backpressure in the classic API (messages buffer in bufferedAmount)
Closed when the tab goes into BFCache and not reconnected automatically

abuse: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking when Origin unchecked

history.change: WebSocket origin check for localhost still permitted
